# Representation and information taxonomy

| Relation | Mathematical signature | Typical loss | Required certificate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coordinate change | Isomorphism within one carrier | None if global | Domain and singularity audit |
| Gauge redundancy | Groupoid action and physical quotient | Local coordinates or sections | Orbit fidelity and observable descent |
| Regulator | Indexed approximation to a target theory | Continuum symmetry or short-distance data | Uniform limit and theory-identity theorem |
| Coarse graining | Generally noninvertible map of states/observables | Microscopic degrees of freedom | Retained-observable fidelity and error modulus |
| Effective description | Domain- and scale-limited theory | Out-of-domain dynamics | Matching, uncertainty, and scale domain |
| Duality | Exact isomorphism of model roots within a domain | Manifest ontology or locality can change | Interpretation and quantity matching |
| Reconstruction | Theorem-generated target from correlation data | Spectral meaning is absent before reconstruction | Positivity, regularity, density, and uniqueness |
| Interpretation | Map from formal structures to physical claims | Underdetermination | Explicit bearers and truth conditions |

## Physical information

“Physical information” is admissible shorthand only for an equivalence class
of distinctions recoverable through a declared family of physical probes.
Its bearer is a state or correlation functional; its equivalence relation is
agreement on a specified physical observable algebra; its accessibility is a
state--observable pairing or an inferential role; and its dynamics is the
action of physical time evolution or scale change on those pairings.  Gauge
changes, RG flow, and time evolution are therefore different typed maps.  If
these data are absent, the paper deletes the word *information* rather than
letting it carry metaphysical weight.
